text: In nineteen-eighteen, Finland fought a civil war. Ask Wikipedia about it, and the answer depends on your language. The Russian article calls the rising a coup. The Finnish one, a power struggle. So which one is right?
Language Mirror compares every language edition of an article. No edition is the truth. Each one is scored against what most editions tell, and checked against the sources.
For the civil war, Finnish and English tell almost the whole shared story. Swedish tells two thirds of it, and cites the least. Every score shows how it is made.

Claude then lists where the editions disagree, quoting each one word for word. Context dot dev reads the cited pages and searches the web for independent sources. Only the German edition ends the war on the fifth of May. The sources say the fifteenth.
The mirror lines up both articles, paragraph by paragraph. Grey is what one side leaves out. Click it, and read it in English.
MariaDB keeps every version with its real edit time, so one query compares the editions in any year. Today, the Ukrainian article is a near copy of the Russian one.
Every paragraph is a vector in a system-versioned MariaDB table with a vector index. Vector search, together with for system time as of, does the matching, the scores and the history.
And it works on any article. Paste a link, and it finds the longest editions: nine for Stepan Bandera, including Polish.
Language Mirror. One story, every Wikipedia. Built on MariaDB at Junction twenty twenty-six.
